"Implement the solution in src/lib.rs so that the tests in tests/forth.rs, tests/alloc-attack.rs pass. The specification follows.

# Instructions

Implement an evaluator for a very simple subset of Forth.

[Forth][forth]
is a stack-based programming language.
Implement a very basic evaluator for a small subset of Forth.

Your evaluator has to support the following words:

- `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` (integer arithmetic)
- `DUP`, `DROP`, `SWAP`, `OVER` (stack manipulation)

Your evaluator also has to support defining new words using the customary syntax: `: word-name definition ;`.

To keep things simple the only data type you need to support is signed integers of at least 16 bits size.

You should use the following rules for the syntax: a number is a sequence of one or more (ASCII) digits, a word is a sequence of one or more letters, digits, symbols or punctuation that is not a number.
(Forth probably uses slightly different rules, but this is close enough.)

Words are case-insensitive.

[forth]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forth_%28programming_language%29


# Instructions append

Note the additional test case in `tests/alloc-attack.rs`. It tests against
algorithmically inefficient implementations. Because of that, it usually times
out online instead of outright failing, leading to a less helpful error message.


Do NOT modify the tests or the build files except as stated below. Do not create new files unless the specification requires them; Helper modules may go under src/; you may add [dependencies] from the offline crates listed in OFFLINE_CRATES.md to Cargo.toml."

## How it works (`src/lib.rs`)

- **Tokenizer**: splits input on whitespace. A run of digits (optionally preceded by `-` when followed by a digit) is a number — so `-1` is a number but `3 -` is the subtraction operator. Everything else is a word, lowercased for case-insensitive lookup. Oversized numbers saturate to `i32` bounds rather than erroring.
- **Dictionary**: a `Vec<Definition>` (builtins + user words) plus a `HashMap<String, usize>` from lowercase name to definition index. Builtins (`+ - * / dup drop swap over`) are the first eight entries, so user words can override them by simply replacing the map entry.
- **Definition-time binding**: when `: name body ;` is parsed, each word in the body is resolved to a definition *index* immediately and stored as `Token::Word(usize)`. This satisfies both tricky tests:
  - `can_use_different_words_with_the_same_name` — `bar` captures the *old* `foo` because it stores the index of the definition that existed at its definition time.
  - `can_define_word_that_uses_word_with_the_same_name` — `: foo foo 1 + ;` binds to the *previous* `foo`, not the new one (no infinite recursion).
- **Lazy execution**: `exec_def` runs definitions iteratively using an explicit frame stack of `(definition index, token position)` pairs — no eager expansion (defeats the alloc attack; each of the 26 chained definitions stores just 2 tokens) and no recursion (deep definition chains can't overflow the call stack).
- **Errors**: `StackUnderflow` when popping an empty stack (checked before the division-by-zero check, so `1 /` underflows and `4 0 /` divides by zero); `DivisionByZero`; `UnknownWord` for undefined words, both at execution and definition time; `InvalidWord` for `: 1 ... ;` (numeric name) and unterminated definitions.

No new files, no dependencies added, and the tests/build files are untouched.
